progressSummary: Audited V3-06 requires repair; WIP baseline preserved when a safe delta existed.

openFindings.problem: The sync pipeline is wired only into the in-memory (test) path. The production SQLite path used on device returns plain SqliteSyncStateRepository and plain Sqlite business repositories: applyDeltas still only buffers pulled records into sync_records (cursor advances) and never materializes them into business tables, and local business writes never call storeLocalRecords, so pushDeltas has no payloads. This is the previous audit's must-fix finding #1, still unfixed for the production path. Additionally, even in the in-memory path only contributions/expenses/todos/settlements are wrapped: writes to persistent_tasks, members, memberships and households never record dirty records.
openFindings.evidence: RepositoryFactory.ts: createSqliteRepositories() constructs syncState: new SqliteSyncStateRepository() and plain Sqlite business repos with no MaterializingSyncState and no sync-recording wrappers; MaterializingSyncState + inline storeLocalRecords wrappers exist only in createInMemoryRepositories(); grep shows storeLocalRecords callers only in RepositoryFactory.ts (in-memory) and the unused SyncRecordingWrapper.ts; pullDeltas/pushDeltas/syncHousehold have zero callers in app/ or src/features; AppContext uses LocalSyncAdapter (honest no-op, isAvailable()===false).
openFindings.requiredFix: Wire the same materialization + dirty-record recording into the SQLite path (e.g. SqliteSyncStateRepository.applyDeltas materializes into Sqlite business tables, and Sqlite business repos record dirty sync records after writes), covering all 8 SYNC_COLLECTIONS including persistent_tasks, members, memberships and households. Add a test that exercises the SQLite repository path (or a shared contract test run against both implementations) proving remote delta -> business record readable + local write -> getDirtyRecords payload.
openFindings.verification: Run the V3-06 e2e suites against the SQLite repository implementation (not only in-memory); assert applyDeltas on SqliteSyncStateRepository leaves the business row readable and a local Sqlite business write appears in getDirtyRecords.

openFindings.problem: applyDeltas does not materialize inside a transaction and advances the cursor before materialization: inner.applyDeltas (which advances the cursor) runs first, then materializeDeltas runs outside any transaction. A failure during materialization leaves the cursor advanced with records present only in the sync_records buffer; the next pull will not re-fetch them, silently losing business data. This violates the criterion 'applyDeltas materializes pulled records into business tables inside a transaction, then advance the cursor'.
openFindings.evidence: MaterializingSyncState.applyDeltas: const applied = await this.inner.applyDeltas(householdId, collection, records); await materializeDeltas(repos, collection, records); return applied; - no withTransaction/withTransactionAsync wrapper around the pair; in-memory withTransaction snapshots only todoRepo and contributionRepo (RepositoryFactory.ts lines 257-266).
openFindings.requiredFix: Wrap cursor advance + materialization in a single transaction (extend in-memory withTransaction snapshot coverage to all affected repos, and use withTransactionAsync on SQLite): materialize first, then advance the cursor, atomically; on failure roll back both so the delta is re-fetched on the next pull.
openFindings.verification: Add a test that injects a failing materialization (e.g. malformed/unsupported payload causing a repo error) and asserts the cursor did not advance and the business tables were not partially updated.

openFindings.problem: Tenant isolation and balance integrity are still not enforced in the data-access path. requireHouseholdMembership, requireRole and assertLedgerWrite have zero callers outside authorizationRules.ts; repositories accept any householdId without any caller-membership context, so a cross-tenant read/write is not blocked at the repository or use-case level. The hostile tests exercise the pure functions directly, not the data-access path. This is the previous audit's must-fix finding #4, still unfixed.
openFindings.evidence: grep -rn 'requireHouseholdMembership|requireRole(|assertLedgerWrite' src/ excluding authorizationRules.ts returns nothing; repositories (InMemoryRepositories.ts, SqliteRepositories.ts) take no userId/membership parameter; hostile tests in v3-06-sync-e2e.test.ts call the rule functions directly rather than through repository reads/writes.
openFindings.requiredFix: Enforce membership scoping in the data-access path: repository or use-case layer must verify the caller's membership for every read/write (e.g. a scoped repository facade taking the caller userId and checking memberships before getByHousehold/create/update/delete), and ledger mutations must go through append/revision/tombstone with assertLedgerWrite-style validation. Hostile tests must prove a non-member read/write is rejected through the actual repository path.
openFindings.verification: Run hostile tests that call the repository path (not the pure functions) with a non-member caller and assert AuthorizationError(CROSS_TENANT) / BALANCE_FALSIFICATION is thrown.

openFindings.problem: Conflict resolution is incomplete and still effectively blind in places. (1) materializeDeltas case 'households' does repos.households.update(record.id, incoming) with no resolveConflict. (2) For the other collections, resolveConflict is called with the local entity fabricated as { id, revision: 0, updatedAt: existing.occurredAt } - local revisions are never tracked, so any remote record with revision >= 1 always wins and a local offline edit of the same id is silently discarded (de facto blind last-write-wins for accounting operations). (3) The SQLite applyDeltas remains blind INSERT OR REPLACE into the buffer.
openFindings.evidence: SyncMaterializer.ts: case 'households': await repos.households.update(record.id, incoming); (no resolveConflict); resolveConflict calls pass revision: 0 for the local side (lines 134-203); SqliteSyncStateRepository.applyDeltas upserts sync_records by id without conflict resolution; the e2e conflict test exercises the pure resolveConflict function, not the materializer path.
openFindings.requiredFix: Track and persist the local revision of each synchronized entity (revision column on business tables or sync metadata), pass the real local revision to resolveConflict in the materializer, apply resolveConflict to households (and members/memberships) as well, and make the SQLite applyDeltas use the same deterministic revision/timestamp/id resolution instead of blind overwrite. Add a materializer-level test where the local revision is higher than the remote and assert the local version wins.
openFindings.verification: Run a materializer-level conflict test (local revision > remote revision on the same id) asserting the local entity is preserved, and a households delta test asserting a remote household update is resolved deterministically rather than blindly overwritten.
